market_forger.title: The Paper Man
market_forger.desc: Deep in the market, a man with no left hand sells permits. "Sixty. The real kind. The submarine hold doesn't check faces, only stamps." He holds a sheet up to the light; the fibre grain matches a genuine one exactly.

buy_papers.outcome: The paper is real and so is the stamp — peeled off a dead man. He folds it and hands it over. "And don't look back at the dock."

refuse.text: Shake your head and walk away
refuse.outcome: You walk off. He calls after you: "Price goes up tomorrow!" You don't look back.

market_organs.title: Your Body Is Currency
market_organs.desc: A man in a lab coat runs "recovery" out of a tarpaulin shelter. He appraises you the way a butcher weighs a cut. "One kidney. Fifty-five. Clean surgery, two hours, you walk out on your own."

sell.outcome: You walk out with fifty-five credits and have to hold the wall to stay upright. The painkillers don't help much. The money does.

walk.outcome: You step out of the shelter and take a deep breath. Lungs still there. Kidney still there.

market_pawn_gun.title: Pawn the Sidearm
market_pawn_gun.desc: The pawnbroker lifts your sidearm between two fingers as if it were something dirty. "Thirty-five. Nobody wants these now. You can't eat a gun."

pawn.outcome: You trade the gun for thirty-five credits and a ticket. Walking out, it hits you that you no longer own a single thing in this city to lean on.

keep.outcome: You holster it again. The broker shrugs. "Your call. Worth less tomorrow anyway."

market_thief.title: The Kid With the Tin
market_thief.desc: A boy no older than ten is held up by the collar, feet kicking, a tin of corned beef clenched in his fist. The stallholder is shouting, "Break his hand!" The boy doesn't cry.

catch.outcome: You pin his wrist. The stallholder kicks him twice and tosses you ten credits for your trouble. When the boy breaks free the tin falls and rolls into the drain.

buy_food.text: Buy the tin and let him go
buy_food.outcome: You pay for it and press a second tin into his hands. He runs a dozen metres, looks back once, then disappears into the crowd.

let_go.outcome: You open your hand and the boy slips into the crowd like a fish. The stallholder curses at you. You ignore him.

market_fake_medicine.title: "Ash Cure"
market_fake_medicine.desc: A stall is piled with garish bottles. "Cures the Ash. Fifteen a bottle. Last course available." The batch number on the base is handwritten and the ink is still wet.

buy.outcome: Your stomach cramps all night. The factory on that batch number burned down three years ago.

refuse.outcome: You put the bottle down and the seller turns immediately to the next customer.

market_dice.title: Dice in the Alley
market_dice.desc: Three men are shooting dice against a wall. One of them pushes the cup towards you. The dice are weighted — you can tell, and they don't mind that you can tell.

roll.outcome: The cup comes up against the wall and all four of you stare at the dice.
roll.win: All red. All three of them swear at once and push thirty-eight across. Your hands are steady when you take it.
roll.lose: All black. You put down the twenty and hear one of them laugh. That laugh follows you down the whole street.

pass.outcome: You wave and walk on. Behind you, the dice hit the ground and someone starts cursing.

market_rumor.title: Word From the Meat Stall
market_rumor.desc: The butcher keeps chopping while he talks. "Heard? The sub changed schedule. Leaves a day early. They don't want too many people knowing." He never looks up.

listen.text: Buy some meat and hear him out
listen.outcome: You spend five credits on half a kilo of something unidentifiable. The rumour is worth more than the meat: the sub really is leaving early.

market_ration.title: Ration Coupons
market_ration.desc: Behind the distribution centre, a man in uniform is buying coupons. "Eighteen each, cash." You know exactly where those coupons come from — the hands of people who didn't make it to today.

sell.outcome: You get eighteen credits. For the next three days you live on water and cigarettes.

share.text: Give them to the old woman in the queue
share.outcome: You press the coupons into the hands of a woman holding an empty pot. She chases you half a block to say thank you. You walk faster.
